Specify a gpfield Gaussian-process model

Source: R/classes.R
gpfield_spec.Rd

Builds the configuration consumed by gp_fit(). A specification fixes the covariance kernel and (for "matern") its smoothness, names the spatial coordinate columns in the data frame the fit will read, optionally names a time column for a spatio-temporal model, and sets the diagonal jitter used to condition the kernel. Nothing is fitted here; the specification is a small, inspectable object so the model is declared before any data are touched.

Usage

gpfield_spec(
  coords,
  response,
  kernel = "matern",
  nu = 1.5,
  time = NA_character_,
  nugget = 1e-06,
  anisotropic = FALSE,
  solver = c("exact", "lowrank"),
  n_inducing = 200L
)

Arguments

coords

Character vector naming the spatial coordinate columns (one for a transect, two for a field, three or more if the caller has projected additional spatial axes). When a time column is also given, it is appended to the coordinate set as an extra, separately-scaled axis.

response

Character scalar naming the response column to smooth.

kernel

Character covariance kernel: "matern" (default) or "se" (squared-exponential).

nu

Matern smoothness; one of 0.5, 1.5 (default) or 2.5. Ignored for the squared-exponential kernel.

time

Optional character scalar naming a time column for a spatio-temporal fit, or NA (default) for a purely spatial model. When a time axis is present the fit is anisotropic by necessity – a unit of space and a unit of time are not exchangeable, so time is given its own length-scale even if anisotropic is left at its default FALSE.

nugget

Positive numeric jitter added to the kernel diagonal for numerical conditioning. Distinct from the estimated observation-noise variance, which is a fitted hyperparameter.

anisotropic

Logical. If TRUE and there are at least two coordinate axes, fit one length-scale per axis (automatic relevance determination) rather than a single isotropic length-scale. The kernel stays isotropic in a per-axis-rescaled coordinate space, so each axis gets its own correlation range – the right model when a field varies on different scales along different directions (an east-west tillage gradient versus a north-south slope, or space versus a time axis). Default FALSE (a single length-scale, the original behaviour).

solver

Character: "exact" (default) fits the exact GP by a full Cholesky factorisation, cubic in the number of observations. "lowrank" fits a Deterministic Training Conditional (DTC) sparse GP on n_inducing space-filling inducing points – cost O(n * n_inducing^2) – for fields too large for the exact solver. The low-rank solver is isotropic (a single length-scale) and falls back to the exact solver when the data have no more rows than n_inducing.

n_inducing

Integer number of inducing points for solver = "lowrank" (default 200, minimum 3); ignored for the exact solver.

Value

A gpfield_spec S7 object.

Details

The default kernel is the "matern" family at nu = 1.5, the usual choice for field data: it is once-differentiable rather than the squared-exponential's infinite smoothness, which avoids the over-smoothing that the squared exponential imposes across real agronomic gradients.

See also

gp_fit(), gp_predict()

Examples

spec <- gpfield_spec(coords = c("x", "y"), response = "yield")
spec
#> <gpfield_spec>
#>   kernel:   matern (nu = 1.5)
#>   coords:   x, y
#>   response: yield

# An anisotropic field: a separate length-scale per axis.
aniso <- gpfield_spec(c("x", "y"), "yield", anisotropic = TRUE)
aniso
#> <gpfield_spec>
#>   kernel:   matern (nu = 1.5) (anisotropic)
#>   coords:   x, y
#>   response: yield

# A large field: the low-rank sparse solver on 150 inducing points.
big <- gpfield_spec(c("x", "y"), "yield", solver = "lowrank",
                    n_inducing = 150L)
big
#> <gpfield_spec>
#>   kernel:   matern (nu = 1.5)
#>   coords:   x, y
#>   response: yield
#>   solver:   low-rank (DTC, 150 inducing points)

# A spatio-temporal specification with the squared-exponential kernel.
st <- gpfield_spec(
  coords = c("x", "y"), response = "ndvi", kernel = "se", time = "doy"
)
st
#> <gpfield_spec>
#>   kernel:   squared-exponential
#>   coords:   x, y
#>   time:     doy
#>   response: ndvi
